title: Juan de Eraso, Spanish ambassador at Genoa, to Philip IV, 18 January 1643 (catalogue 755): the Grand Duke of Tuscany holds back

plaintext.source: Plain original EST,LEG,3598,42 exists but is not online (PARES shows no. 41 under it); not used.
Contemporary plain original 3598,290; used only to validate the key.

system.summary: the 1643 cipher of the Genoa embassy (a different table from that of 1638): syllabic series of five numbers (27 fa, 32 ta, 37 as, 42 na, 47 ja, 52 al, 57 da, 62 an), disguised bigrams (ax = la, at = sa, ha = ma, am = ya), trigrams (sal = ra, gan = ca, tes = ve, las = tra), single letters (ℓ = a, c = n, v = e) and code (270 = Vuestra Majestad, 223 = república, 180 = Francia)

prior_solution.where: Catalogue 755 open for 1643-1651; no target folder for these letters; the plain original of 3598,44 is not online.

conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout chose the target from the catalogue and set the rules (frozen key before validation, held-out checks, prior-work search the day of publication); AI agents transcribed, solved, checked and wrote up. Doubtful signs were settled by targeted visual review where stated.
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout

solution.what: Inventory of the ten 1643-1651 items of no. 755 via PARES lists sorted by shelfmark: nine have their plain text in the bundle.
Key learned on 3598,38/37 and 41/40 by seeded EM alignment, frozen.
Held-out test 15 vs 14: 0.816 chars / 0.750 words, below the pre-set criterion; reported.
Main held-out test 291 vs plain original 290 (pair designated before opening): 0.881 chars / 0.834 words vs control p99 0.298 / 0.121.
3598,44 transcribed and read with K4b; code words restored from the sense where noted.

outcome.method: key recovered based on plaintext from external sources
outcome.method_basis: Key learned from other letters of the same cipher with their contemporary plain originals, validated on a held-out pair, then applied to 3598,44.
outcome.fraction_read_source: 137 words in the cipher portion: 115 certain, 4 probable, 16 restored from the sense, 2 unresolved (codes 149, 210).

credits.note: key learned and validated on a held-out pair; 3598,44 read, Spanish text and English translation

texts.label: Juan de Eraso to Philip IV, Genoa, 18 January 1643 (AGS EST,LEG,3598,44)
texts.summary: January 1643: Tortona has just been retaken, the war with France weighs on the Milanese, and Madrid is pressing the Italian princes bound to Spain to send troops. The ambassador at Genoa, Juan de Eraso, has forwarded the King’s letter to Grand Duke Ferdinand II de’ Medici. The answer comes back: the Grand Duke refers the matter to his resident in Madrid. Eraso tells the King, in cipher, that this is a way of playing for time.

reading_review.note: reading.md and translation.md read as sentences: four chancery sentences (the Grand Duke's answer to Eraso's letter, the copy sent with it, why the reference to the resident in Madrid gains him time, the report sent at once). The two holes (149 before 'residente', 210 before 'antes este aviso') do not stop any sentence parsing; the 16 restored code words are marked [x] and justified one by one in NOTES. Plain-text opening and closing are in italics.

texts.label: Held-out validation letter: Eraso to Philip IV, Genoa, 15 October 1643 (AGS EST,LEG,3598,291 p. 1, with the contemporary plain original 3598,290)
texts.note: Test material, not a reading: the transcription of 3598,291 p. 1 and the contemporary plain original 3598,290 it was scored against (0.881 of characters, 0.834 of words).

validation.notes: Contributor's pre-registered held-out test (not docs/_validate.py): key K4b frozen, then scored on 3598,291 p. 1 against its contemporary plain original 3598,290: 0.881 of characters, 0.834 of words, against p99 0.298 / 0.121 for 200 permuted-value control keys; criterion (0.85 / 0.75) met. The first held-out test (3598,15 vs 14) gave 0.816 / 0.750 and was reported as below the criterion.
